question.text: Mr. Arvind Sharma, a family-office CIO, is evaluating the DIFFERENT channels through which his INR 80 crore allocation can be deployed into Indian markets. Per NISM Ch 2.4, which list correctly identifies the five managed-portfolio channels available in India?

answer.text: Mutual Funds, Collective Investment Schemes, Portfolio Management Services, Alternative Investment Funds, Specialized Investment Funds
Mutual Funds, ULIPs, NPS, Bank FDs, Corporate FDs
PMS, AIF, Hedge Funds, Private Banking, Family Office
Only Mutual Funds and AIFs — all other channels are for retail investors only

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 2.4.2, the five managed-portfolio channels listed in the NISM syllabus are: Mutual Funds, Collective Investment Schemes (CIS), Portfolio Management Services (PMS), Alternative Investment Funds (AIF), and Specialized Investment Funds (SIF — introduced vide SEBI amendment w.e.f. Dec 16, 2024, with INR 10 lakh minimum). The Trap: Option B includes ULIPs and FDs which are not 'managed portfolio' vehicles in the NISM channel taxonomy — ULIPs are insurance-linked, FDs are direct bank products. Option C lists wrappers (private banking, family office) which are distribution channels, not product channels. Option D is false. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A distributor tests MF/PMS/AIF/CIS; XXI-A tests PMS specifically; XIX-C as manager exam tests the full channel taxonomy for platform strategy decisions. Manager's Pro-Tip: When advising a family office on which wrapper to use, map objective → channel. Liquidity need + retail ticket = MF. HNI + tailored discretion = PMS. Sophisticated + illiquid = AIF. Sophisticated + MF-wrapper + INR 10L minimum = SIF. Most managers underuse SIF — it's the newest arrow in the quiver.
